steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Whatever comes first in the sentence, the conjugated verb MUST be second. If something other than the subject comes first, the subject swaps places with the verb (verb-subject inversion).

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: When a subordinate clause comes FIRST in the sentence, the main clause that follows has VERB-FIRST-SUBJECT order: "Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause" (NOT "ich bleibe"). The subordinate clause counts as position 1, so the verb of the main clause must be in position 2.

steps.title: German Exam Tips — Word Order and Conjunctions
steps.body: 1. For Word Order and Conjunctions, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Word Order and Conjunctions, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Rewrite with correct word order: Ich denke (dass / Deutsch / wichtig / sein). Ich bleibe zu Hause (weil / ich / krank / sein). | Q: Rewrite starting with the subordinate clause: Ich gehe nicht aus, weil das Wetter schlecht ist. → Weil...

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Ich denke, dass Deutsch wichtig ist. Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin. (Verb goes to the END after dass and weil.) | Weil das Wetter schlecht ist, gehe ich nicht aus. (Subordinate clause first = position 1; main clause verb must be in position 2 = gehe ich, NOT ich gehe.)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use a range of tenses (present, past, future) to access higher marks Include opinions with reasons (ich finde... weil... / meiner Meinung nach...) Check case endings (nominative, accusative, dative) before finishing Get word order right: verb-second in main clauses, verb-at-end after dass/weil/wenn Use complex structures: subordinate clauses, modal verbs, separable verbs Include cultural references to German-speaking countries (DACH)
